crux: 3D tilt of the head-tail axis in the glide: along the flight axis (C1/C2, ~0.9 m depth spread, ~1.0 m+snout) vs tilted ~15 deg (round 1, ~0.5 m spread, 0.74 m chord) vs planar (DeepSeek)
fault_found: C1's on-flight-axis geometry predicts the head-tail image vector shrinks to 205 px by frame 71; measured 223 px (rigid head-foot pair shrinks exactly at the root-depth rate 0.881), so C1's ~1.0 m head-tail chord is wrong; my triangulation gives 0.74-0.80 m, frame 0 gives ~0.77-0.83 m, +0.10 snout
lesson: When a body seen nearly end-on translates rigidly, compare how fast the image vector between its two ends shrinks with how fast a short rigid pair at equal depth shrinks: the excess shrink measures the depth spread of the ends and decides between an along-the-motion-axis assumption and a tilted body, without needing any per-point triangulation.
